chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah have mercy on him) said: He narrated from al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Aban, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Fadala, from al-Aban, from Zurara, from Hamran, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him)
regarding the saying of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He: "Then, let them end their tafath"
He said: Tafath is the abstention of the man from perfume. When he has completed his rites, perfume becomes permissible to him.
ai.seo_question: What does the term 'tafath' mean in the context of Hajj rituals according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that 'tafath' refers specifically to the removal of perfume scent from the body, distinguishing it from the general state of ihram. It establishes the legal principle that the prohibition on perfume is lifted immediately upon the completion of the core Hajj rites, reflecting the Shia emphasis on precise ritual purification. This interpretation aligns with the broader Quranic theme of removing impurities to attain spiritual purity.
